Financial Group, Inc. is the parent holding company for Savings Institute Bank and Trust Company (the "Bank").  The Bank operates as a community-oriented financial institution offering a full range of financial services to consumers and businesses in its market area, including life insurance and annuities.&#160;&#160;The Bank attracts deposits from the general public and uses those funds to originate one- to four-family residential, multi-family and commercial real estate, commercial business (including time share lending, loans to condominium associations and medical loans) and consumer loans.&#160;&#160;The Bank also purchases commercial business loans, including loans fully guaranteed by the Small Business Administration (the "SBA") and the United States Department of Agriculture (the "USDA").  The Bank sells certain fixed-rate one- to four-family residential conforming loans the Bank originates in the secondary market, primarily with the servicing retained.&#160;&#160;Such sales generate mortgage banking fee income.&#160;&#160;The remainder of the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio is originated for investment.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">On September 6, 2013, the Company acquired Newport Bancorp, Inc. ("Newport"), the holding company for Newport Federal Savings Bank for 2,683,099 shares of Company common stock and $30.9 million in cash.  Based upon the Company's $11.22 per share closing price on September 6, 2013, the transaction was valued at approximately $61.0 million.  As a result of this transaction, the Company added six branches, $446.4 million in assets, $361.1 million in loans and $288.4 million in deposits to its franchise. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Market Area and Competition</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Company is headquartered in Willimantic, Connecticut, which is located in eastern Connecticut approximately 30 miles east of Hartford.&#160;&#160;The Bank operates </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">24</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;full-service offices throughout Windham, New London, Tolland, Hartford and Middlesex counties in Connecticut and Newport and Washington counties in Rhode Island.&#160;&#160;Most of the Bank&#8217;s deposit customers reside in the areas surrounding the Bank&#8217;s branch offices.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s primary lending area is eastern Connecticut and Rhode Island with additional concentrations in Massachusetts and New Hampshire.  The economy in the Company&#8217;s Connecticut market area is relatively diverse and primarily oriented to the educational, service, entertainment, insurance, manufacturing and retail industries.&#160;&#160;The major employers in our Connecticut market area include several hospitals, institutions of higher education, the Mohegan Sun and Foxwoods casinos, Aetna Insurance Company, Inc. and General Dynamics Defense Systems.&#160;&#160;In addition, there are also many small to mid-sized businesses that support the local economy.  The economy in the Company's Rhode Island market area is primarily oriented to the health care, educational, retail and hospitality industries.  The major employers in the Rhode Island area include several hospitals, universities and pharmaceutical manufacturers.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Windham, New London, Tolland, Hartford and Middlesex counties in Connecticut have a total population of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">1.6 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">622,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;total households, according to SNL Financial. &#160;For </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, median household income levels ranged from </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$70,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;to </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$87,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;in the five counties we maintain branch offices in Connecticut, compared to </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$77,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;for Connecticut and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$61,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;for the United States, according to published statistics.  Newport and Washington counties in Rhode Island have a total population and total households of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">209,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">85,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, respectively, according to SNL Financial.  Median household income levels in Newport and Washington counties for </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font Bank faces significant competition for the attraction of deposits and origination of loans.&#160;&#160;The most direct competition for deposits has historically come from several financial institutions operating in the Bank&#8217;s market area and, to a lesser extent, from other financial service companies, such as brokerage firms, credit unions and insurance companies.&#160;&#160;The Bank also faces competition for investors&#8217; funds from money market funds and other corporate and government securities.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">June&#160;30, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, which is the most recent date for which data is available from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the &#8220;FDIC&#8221;), the Bank held </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">24.20%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;of the deposits in Windham County, Connecticut, which is the largest market share out of the </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">10</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;financial institutions with offices in this county.&#160;&#160;Also, at </font><font </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">1.13%</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;of the deposits in New London, Tolland, Hartford and Middlesex counties, Connecticut, which is the </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">14th</font><font in these counties.&#160;&#160;In Rhode Island, at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">June&#160;30, 2017</font><font large national or regional bank holding companies also operate in the Bank&#8217;s Connecticut and Rhode Island market areas.&#160; These institutions are significantly larger and, therefore, have significantly greater resources and may offer products and services that the Bank does not provide. &#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank&#8217;s competition for loans comes primarily from financial institutions in its market area, and, to a lesser extent, from other financial service providers, such as mortgage companies and mortgage brokers.  Competition </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">4</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">for loans also comes from the increasing number of non-depository financial service companies entering the  mortgage market, such as insurance companies, securities companies and specialty finance companies.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank expects competition to increase in the future as a result of legislative, regulatory and technological changes and the continuing trend of consolidation in the financial services industry.  Technological advances, for example, have lowered barriers to entry, allowed banks to expand their geographic reach by providing services over the Internet and made it possible for non-depository institutions to offer products and services that traditionally have been provided by banks.  Changes in federal law permit affiliation among banks, securities firms and insurance companies, which promotes a competitive environment in the financial services industry. Competition for deposits and the origination of loans could limit the Company&#8217;s growth in the future.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div><a name="sBE3455F616AE5DB1A2B8EAA64EE9B98F"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Risk Management</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;&#32;Managing risk is an essential part of successfully managing a financial institution.  Our most prominent risk exposures are credit risk, interest rate risk and market risk.  Credit risk is the risk of not collecting the interest and/or the principal balance of a loan or investment when it is due.  Interest rate risk is the potential reduction of net interest income as a result of changes in interest rates.  Market risk arises from fluctuations in interest rates that may result in changes in the values of financial instruments, such as available for sale securities, that are accounted for on a mark-to-market basis.  Other risks the Company faces are operational risks, liquidity risks and reputation risk.  Operational risks include risks related to fraud, regulatory compliance, processing errors, cyber security, technology and disaster recovery.  Liquidity risk is the possible inability to fund obligations to depositors, lenders or borrowers or for the Company to pay its obligations as they become due as a result of unforeseen circumstances.  Reputation risk is the risk negative publicity or press, whether true or not, could cause a decline in the Company&#8217;s customer base or revenue.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Credit Risk Management.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;&#32;Our strategy for credit risk management focuses on having well-defined credit policies and uniform underwriting criteria and providing prompt attention to potential problem loans.  The Company has strengthened its oversight of problem assets by maintaining a Managed Assets Committee.  The Committee, which consists of our Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and other loan and credit administration officers, meets quarterly to review classified and watch list credits to ensure the appropriateness of the current classification and to attempt to identify any new problem loans.  The Board of Directors reviews the Committee&#8217;s reports on a quarterly basis.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div><a name="sA3A6D2F26A8C5F43A5E10A7075B6D013"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Lending Activities</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;&#32;The Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio consists primarily of one- to four-family residential mortgage loans, multi-family and commercial real estate loans and commercial business loans.  To a much lesser extent, the loan portfolio includes construction and consumer loans.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the Bank had loans held for sale totaling </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$835,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">One- to Four-Family Residential Loans</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">One of the Bank&#8217;s primary lending activities is the origination of mortgage loans to enable borrowers to purchase or refinance existing homes or to construct new residential dwellings in its market area.&#160;&#160;The Bank offers fixed-rate loans with terms of 10, 15, 20 or 30 years.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s adjustable-rate mortgage loans are based primarily on 30-year amortization schedules.&#160;&#160;Interest rates and payments on adjustable-rate mortgage loans adjust annually after a one, three, five, seven or ten-year initial fixed period.&#160;&#160;Borrower demand for adjustable-rate loans versus fixed-rate loans is a function of the level of current and anticipated future interest rates, the difference between the interest rates and loan fees offered for fixed-rate mortgage loans and the initial period interest rates and loan fees for adjustable-rate loans.  The relative amount of fixed-rate mortgage loans and adjustable-rate mortgage loans that can be originated at any time is largely determined by the demand for each in a competitive environment and the effect each has on the Bank&#8217;s interest rate risk.&#160;&#160;The loan fees charged, interest rates and other provisions of mortgage loans are determined on the basis of the Bank&#8217;s pricing criteria and competitive market conditions.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Generally, the Bank does not originate conventional mortgage loans with loan-to-value ratios exceeding 95% and generally originates loans with a loan-to-value ratio in excess of 80% only when secured by first liens on owner-occupied one- to four-family residences.&#160;&#160;Mortgage loans with loan-to-value ratios in excess of 80% generally require private mortgage insurance or additional collateral.&#160;&#160;The Bank requires all properties securing mortgage loans to be appraised by a board approved independent licensed appraiser and requires title insurance on all first </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">6</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Borrowers must obtain hazard insurance and flood insurance for loans on properties located in a flood zone before closing the loan.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">In an effort to provide financing for moderate income and first-time buyers, the Bank offers loans insured by the Federal Housing Administration and the Veterans Administration and participates in the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority Program.&#160;&#160;The Bank also offers Guaranteed Rural Housing Loans through the USDA.  The Bank offers fixed-rate residential mortgage loans through these programs to qualified individuals and originates the loans using modified underwriting guidelines.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Multi-Family and Commercial Real Estate Loans</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The origination of multi-family and commercial real estate ("CRE") loans is another primary lending activity of the Bank.  Such loans are made throughout its market area and in strategic areas in the surrounding region for the purpose of acquiring, developing, improving or refinancing multi-family and commercial real estate where the property is the primary collateral securing the loan, and the income generated from the property is the primary repayment source.&#160;&#160;The Bank offers fixed-rate and adjustable-rate multi-family and commercial real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Adjustable-rate multi-family and commercial real estate loans originate for amortization periods up to 25 years.&#160;&#160;The Bank may originate loans with 30-year amortization periods in investment commercial real estate and commercial bond finance loan categories only.  Interest rates and payments on these loans typically adjust every five years after a five-year initial fixed-rate period.  The Bank&#8217;s multi-family and commercial real estate loans are generally secured by owner-occupied properties, including churches and retail facilities. These loans are secured by first mortgages that generally do not exceed 75% of the property&#8217;s appraised value.&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank intends to continue to emphasize making these types of loans, as market conditions permit, as such loans produce yields that are generally higher than one- to four-family residential loans and are more sensitive to changes in market interest rates.  At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the largest outstanding multi-family or commercial real estate loan was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$16.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.&#160;&#160;This loan is secured by a single tenant retail property and was performing according to its terms at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank maintains an Out-of-Market CRE Market Lending Program.  The primary focus of this program is to develop greater investment in commercial real estate loans in the metro-Boston area and the surrounding region.  The Bank employs a highly seasoned senior commercial real estate loan officer with significant expertise in lending in this region.  Loans originated in this lending area comprise income producing properties representing office, flex, industrial, retail, single credit tenant and residential apartments.  These properties have strong income support, favorable demographics and are owned and managed by experienced and financially strong property managers.  These loans are predominately shorter-term loan facilities (generally 5-year maturities), which are structured to provide the Bank with strong asset growth, coupled with a focus on credit quality and interest rate risk management.  At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the Bank's exposure in Out-of-Market CRE Market Lending was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$192.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Construction and Land Loans.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank originates loans to individuals, and to a lesser extent, builders, to finance construction of residential dwellings.&#160;&#160;The Bank also originates construction loans for commercial development projects, including condominiums, apartment buildings, single-family subdivisions as well as owner-occupied properties used for businesses.&#160;&#160;Residential construction loans generally provide for the payment of interest only during the construction phase, which is usually twelve months.&#160;&#160;At the end of the construction phase, the loan generally converts to a permanent mortgage loan.&#160;&#160;Commercial construction loans generally provide for the payment of interest only during the construction phase, which may range from three to twenty-four months.  Loans generally can be made with a maximum loan-to-value ratio of 80% on residential construction, 75% on construction for nonresidential properties and 80% of the lesser of the appraised value or cost of the project on multi-family construction.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the largest outstanding commercial construction loan commitment was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$8.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;for the construction of a sports complex, of which </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$7.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;was outstanding and the largest residential construction loan commitment was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$950,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, all of which was outstanding.&#160;&#160;These loans were performing according to their terms at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.&#160;&#160;Primarily all commitments to fund construction </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">7</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">loans require an appraisal of the property by a board approved independent licensed appraiser.&#160;&#160;Also, inspections of the property are required before the disbursement of funds during the term of the construction loan.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank also originates development land loans to individuals, local contractors and developers to make improvements on approved building lots, subdivisions and condominium projects within two years of the date of the loan.&#160;&#160;Such loans to individuals generally are written with a maximum loan-to-value ratio based upon the appraised value or purchase price of the land.&#160;&#160;Maximum loan-to-value ratio on raw land is 50%, while the maximum loan-to-value ratio for land development loans involving approved projects is 65%.&#160;&#160;The Bank offers fixed-rate land loans and variable-rate land loans that adjust monthly.&#160;&#160;Land loans totaled </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$1.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commercial Business Loans.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;The Bank originates commercial business loans to a variety of professionals, sole proprietorships and small businesses primarily in its market area.&#160;&#160;When originating commercial business loans, the Bank considers the financial statements of the borrower, the borrower&#8217;s payment history of both corporate and personal debt, the debt service capabilities of the borrower, the projected cash flows of the business, the viability of the industry in which the customer operates and the value of the collateral.  At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the largest outstanding commercial loan was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$15.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, which is a general obligation bond to a private college and is further secured by a pledge of the unrestricted receipts, revenues, income and other monies of the college.&#160;&#160;This loan was performing according to its terms at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">These loans are generally secured by business assets other than real estate, such as business equipment and inventory, in conformance to policy established borrowing base limits. &#160;The Bank originates one-year revolving credit facilities to finance short-term working capital needs of businesses to be repaid by business cash flow.  In addition, the Bank originates non-revolving credit facilities to provide a period of time during which the business can borrow funds for planned equipment purchases and other improvement expenditures.&#160;&#160;These loans convert to a term loan at the expiration of a draw period, which is not to exceed twelve months, and will be paid over a predefined amortization period.&#160;&#160;Additional products such as time notes, letters of credit and equipment lease financing are offered.  Additionally, the Bank may purchase the portion of commercial business loans that are fully guaranteed by the SBA or the USDA.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, purchased SBA and USDA loans totaled </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$89.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank utilizes experienced loan officers and staff to offer specialized lending programs to finance capital improvements for residential and commercial condominium associations as well as the time share industry.  Condominium association loans are secured with the assigned right to levy and collect special assessments from the individual unit owners.  The condominium association loan portfolio consists of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">68</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;loans totaling </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$27.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;as of </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.  The Bank is not involved with the development of time share resorts, but provides financing for investors with loans secured by diverse consumer receivables.  The Bank's exposure in time share lending was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">16</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;loans totaling </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$50.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Consumer Loans</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank offers a variety of consumer loans, primarily home equity lines of credit, and, to a lesser extent, loans secured by marketable securities, passbook or certificate accounts, motorcycles, automobiles and recreational vehicles.&#160;&#160;Generally, the Bank offers automobile loans with a maximum loan-to-value ratio of 100% of the purchase price for new vehicles.&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The procedures for underwriting consumer loans include an assessment of the applicant&#8217;s payment history on other debts and their ability to meet existing obligations and payments on the proposed loans.  Although the applicant&#8217;s creditworthiness is a primary consideration, the underwriting process also includes a comparison of the value of the collateral, if any, to the proposed loan amount.&#160;&#160;Home equity lines of credit have adjustable rates of interest that are indexed to the prime rate as reported in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">The Wall Street Journal</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.&#160;&#160;A home equity line of credit may be drawn down by the borrower for a period of nine years and ten months from the date of the loan agreement.   During this period, the borrower is only required to make interest-only payments.&#160;&#160;The borrower has to pay back the amount outstanding under the line of credit over a term not to exceed fifteen years, beginning at the end of the nine-year and ten month period.&#160;&#160;The Bank will offer home equity loans with a maximum combined loan-to-value ratio of 80%.</font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">8</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Underwriting Risks.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#160;&#160;While the Bank anticipates that adjustable-rate loans will better offset the adverse effects of an increase in interest rates as compared to fixed-rate mortgages, the increased mortgage payments required of adjustable-rate loan borrowers in a rising interest rate environment could cause an increase in delinquencies and defaults.&#160;&#160;The marketability and collateral value of the underlying property also may be adversely affected in a high interest rate environment.&#160;&#160;In addition, although adjustable-rate mortgage loans help make the Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio more responsive to changes in interest rates, the extent of this interest sensitivity is limited by annual and lifetime interest rate adjustment limits.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Loans secured by multi-family and commercial real estate generally have larger balances and involve a greater degree of risk than one- to four-family residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Additionally, many of our multi-family and commercial real estate borrowers have more than one loan outstanding with us.  Consequently, an adverse development with respect to one loan or one credit relationship can expose us to a significantly greater risk of loss compared to an adverse development with respect to a residential mortgage loan.  Of primary concern in multi-family and commercial real estate lending is the borrower&#8217;s creditworthiness and the feasibility and cash flow potential of the project.  Payments on loans secured by income-producing properties often depend on the successful operation and management of the properties.  As a result, repayment of such loans may be subject, to a greater extent than residential real estate loans, to adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy.  To monitor cash flows on income-producing properties, the Bank generally requires borrowers and loan guarantors to provide annual financial statements and/or tax returns.&#160;&#160;In reaching a decision on whether to make a multi-family or commercial real estate loan, consideration is given to the net operating income of the property, the borrower&#8217;s expertise, credit history and the profitability and value of the underlying property.&#160;&#160;The Bank generally requires that the properties securing these real estate loans have debt service coverage ratios (the ratio of earnings before debt service to debt service) of at least 1.20.&#160;&#160;Environmental screens, surveys and inspections are obtained when circumstances suggest the possibility of the presence of hazardous materials.  Further, in connection with the ongoing monitoring of the loan, the Bank typically reviews the property, the underlying loan and guarantors annually.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Construction financing is generally considered to involve a higher degree of risk of loss than long-term financing on improved, occupied real estate.&#160;&#160;Risk of loss on a construction loan depends largely upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the property&#8217;s value at completion of construction, the estimated cost (including interest) of construction and the ability of the project to be sold upon completion.&#160;&#160;During the construction phase, a number of factors could result in delays and cost overruns.&#160;&#160;If the estimate of construction costs proves to be inaccurate, the Bank may be required to advance funds beyond the amount originally committed to permit completion of the building.&#160;&#160;If the estimate of value proves to be inaccurate, the Bank may be confronted, at or before the maturity of the loan, with a building having a value that is insufficient to assure full repayment.&#160;&#160;If the Bank is forced to foreclose on a building before or at completion due to a borrower default, the Bank may not be able to recover all of the unpaid balance of, and accrued interest on, the loan as well as related foreclosure and holding costs.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Unlike residential mortgage loans, which generally are made on the basis of the borrower&#8217;s ability to make repayment from his or her employment or other income, and which are secured by real property the value of which tends to be more easily ascertainable, commercial business loans are of higher risk and typically are made on the basis of the borrower&#8217;s ability to make repayment from the cash flows of the borrower&#8217;s underlying business.&#160;&#160;As a result, the availability of funds for the repayment of commercial business loans may depend substantially on the success of the business itself.&#160;&#160;Further, any collateral securing such loans may depreciate over time, may be difficult to appraise and may fluctuate in value.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Consumer loans entail greater risk than residential mortgage loans, particularly in the case of consumer loans that are unsecured or secured by assets that depreciate rapidly.&#160;&#160;In such cases, repossessed collateral for a defaulted consumer loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment for the outstanding loan and the remaining deficiency often does not warrant significant collection efforts against the borrower.&#160;&#160;In addition, consumer loan collections depend on the borrower&#8217;s continuing financial stability, and therefore are more likely to be adversely </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">9</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">affected by job loss, divorce, illness or personal bankruptcy.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, the application of various federal and state laws, including bankruptcy and insolvency laws, may limit the amount which can be recovered on such loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Originations, Purchases, Sales and Servicing</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Loan originations come from a number of sources.&#160;&#160;The primary source of loan originations are the Bank&#8217;s in-house loan originators, and, to a lesser extent, advertising and referrals from customers.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank may purchase portions of loans that are fully guaranteed by the SBA or the USDA.&#160;&#160;The loans are primarily for commercial and agricultural properties located throughout the United States.&#160;&#160;The Bank did not purchase such loans during the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;or 2016.  There were no sales of SBA and USDA loans for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank purchased </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$36.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$37.7 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;of multi-family and commercial real estate loans and other commercial business loans in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, respectively, which included primarily participation loans and medical loans.  The Bank performs its own underwriting analysis before purchasing a loan and, therefore, believes there should not be a greater risk of default on these obligations compared to loans the Bank originates itself.&#160;&#160;However, in a purchased loan, the Bank does not service the loan and thus is subject to the policies and practices of the originating lender with regard to monitoring delinquencies, pursuing collections and instituting foreclosure proceedings.  Participation loans are entered into by the Bank with other institutions.  Total participation loans entered into by the Bank were </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$25.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;for both </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.  Medical loans are purchased from a company specializing in medical loan originations.  Medical loans are commercial business loans secured by medical equipment and are primarily out of our market area.  Total medical loans purchased were </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$10.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$10.7 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;in </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, respectively.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank originates conventional conforming one- to four-family loans which meet Fannie Mae underwriting standards.&#160;&#160;The Bank sells certain fixed-rate one- to four-family residential conforming loans in the secondary market, primarily on a servicing retained basis.&#160;&#160;Such loans are sold to Fannie Mae, the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority, the Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston (the "FHLB") under the Mortgage Partnership Finance Program and other third-party correspondents.&#160;&#160;The decision to sell loans in the secondary market is based on prevailing market interest rate conditions, an analysis of the composition and risk of the loan portfolio, liquidity needs and interest rate risk management.&#160;&#160;Generally, loans are sold without recourse.&#160;&#160;The Bank utilizes the proceeds from these sales primarily to meet liquidity needs.  Proceeds from the sale of one- to four-family loans totaled </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$54.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$38.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;for the years ended </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">2016</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, respectively.  The Bank intends to continue to originate these types of loans for sale in the secondary market in the future to increase its noninterest income.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the Bank retained the servicing rights on </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$248.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;of loans, consisting primarily of fixed-rate mortgage loans sold with or without recourse to third parties.&#160;&#160;Loan repurchase commitments are agreements to repurchase loans previously sold upon the occurrence of conditions established in the contract, including default by the underlying borrower.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the exposure amount for loans sold with recourse totaled </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$1,000</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.&#160;&#160;Loan servicing includes collecting and remitting loan payments, accounting for principal and interest, contacting delinquent mortgagors, processing insurance and tax payments on behalf of borrowers, assisting in foreclosures and property dispositions when necessary and general administration of loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Approval Procedures and Authority</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank&#8217;s lending activities follow written, non-discriminatory,</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">underwriting standards and loan origination procedures established by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors and</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">management.  All residential mortgages and home equity lines of credit in excess of $10.0 million or other consumer loans in excess of $4.0 million require the approval of the Board of</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Directors.  The Loan Committee of the Board of Directors has the authority to approve: (1) residential mortgage</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">loans and consumer home equity lines of credit up to $10.0 million, (2) commercial loans up to the regulatory legal lending limit, and (3) consumer loans up to $4.0 million.  The Credit Committee, which consists of members of management, has authority to approve: (1) residential mortgage</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">loans and consumer home equity lines of credit up to $4.0 million, (2) commercial loans up to $8.0 million, and (3) consumer loans up to $2.0 million.  The President and Chief Lending Officer have approval authority for: (1) residential mortgage loans</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">that conform to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac standards up to $4.0 million or $417,000 for those that are nonconforming</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">, </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">(2) home equity lines of credit up to $4.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">,</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">&#32;and (3) consumer loans up to</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$250,000 individually or $1.0 million jointly.  The President and Chief Lending Officer have approval authority for commercial real estate and other commercial loans up to $1.0 million individually or $2.0 million jointly.&#160; Additionally, certain loan</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">and branch administration personnel have the authority to approve residential mortgage loans, home equity lines and consumer</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;color:#1f497d;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">loans up to certain limits as specified in the Bank's loan policy.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loans to One Borrower</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The maximum amount that the Bank may lend to one borrower and the borrower&#8217;s related entities is limited, by regulation, to 15% of the Bank&#8217;s stated capital and reserves.&#160;&#160;At </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, the Bank&#8217;s general regulatory limit on loans to one borrower was approximately </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$24.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.&#160;&#160;At that date, the Bank&#8217;s largest lending relationship was </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">$20.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">, representing commercial real estate loans on office buildings.&#160;&#160;These loans were performing according to their original terms at </font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2017</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Commitments</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank issues commitments for fixed- and adjustable-rate mortgage loans conditioned upon the occurrence of certain events.&#160;&#160;Commitments to originate mortgage loans are legally binding agreements </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">13</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">to lend to customers.&#160;&#160;Generally, our mortgage loan commitments expire in 60 days or less from the date of the application.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Delinquencies</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">When a borrower fails to make a required loan payment, the Bank takes a number of steps to have the borrower cure the delinquency and restore the loan to current status.&#160;&#160;The Bank makes initial contact with the borrower when the loan becomes 15 days past due.&#160;&#160;If payment is not then received by the 30th day of delinquency, additional letters and phone calls generally are made.  When the loan becomes 90 days past due, a letter is sent notifying the borrower foreclosure proceedings will commence if the loan is not brought current within 30 days.&#160;&#160;Generally, when the loan becomes 120 days past due, the Bank will commence foreclosure proceedings against any real property that secures the loan or attempt to repossess any personal property that secures a consumer or commercial loan.&#160;&#160;If a foreclosure action is instituted and the loan is not brought current, paid in full or refinanced before the foreclosure sale, the real property securing the loan is typically sold at foreclosure.&#160;&#160;The Bank may consider loan repayment arrangements with certain borrowers under certain circumstances.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font loans in foreclosure and all foreclosed and repossessed property that the Bank owns.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Classified Assets.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">Management of the Bank, including the Managed Asset Committee, consisting of a number of the Bank&#8217;s officers, review and classify the assets of the Bank on a monthly basis and the Board of Directors reviews the results of the reports on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;Federal regulations and the Bank&#8217;s internal policies require that management utilize an internal asset classification system to monitor and evaluate the credit risk inherent in its loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Bank's regulators have the authority to identify problem assets and, if </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">14</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">appropriate, require them to be classified.&#160;&#160;There are three classifications for problem assets; substandard, doubtful and loss. &#8220;Substandard assets&#8221; must have one or more defined weaknesses and are characterized by the distinct possibility that the Bank will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Doubtful assets&#8221; have all the weaknesses inherent in those classified as &#8220;substandard&#8221; with the additional characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions and values questionable, and there is a high probability of loss.&#160;&#160;Assets classified as &#8220;loss&#8221; are those assets considered uncollectible and of such little value that continuance as assets of the institution are not warranted.&#160;&#160;The regulations also provide for a &#8220;special mention&#8221; category, described as assets which do not currently expose  the Bank to a sufficient degree of risk to warrant classification but do possess credit deficiencies or potential weakness deserving close attention.&#160;&#160;If the Bank classifies an asset as a loss, a loan loss allowance in the amount of 100% of the portion of the asset classified as a loss is established or the loan is fully charged-off.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Nonperforming Assets and Restructured Loans.&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank considers repossessed assets and loans that are 90 days or more past due to be nonperforming assets.&#160;&#160;Loans are generally placed on nonaccrual status when they become 90 days delinquent at which time the accrual of interest ceases and any previously recorded interest is reversed and recorded as a reduction of loan interest and fee income.&#160;&#160;Typically, payments received on a nonaccrual loan are applied to the outstanding principal and interest balance as determined at the time of collection of the loan.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">The Bank periodically may agree to modify the contractual terms of loans.&#160;&#160;When a loan is modified and concessions have been made to the original contractual terms, such as reductions of interest rates or deferral of interest or principal payments, due to the borrower&#8217;s financial condition, the modification is considered a troubled debt restructuring (&#8220;TDR&#8221;).&#160;&#160;All TDRs are initially classified as impaired.  The Bank adheres to its nonaccrual policy </font></div><div><br></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:10pt;">15</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;" href="#s9B314409A8CD51CCB77E21EF057C50D6"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Table of Contents</font></a></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;">for all TDR loans.  Loans that were current prior to modification would not require nonaccrual status subsequent to the modification. If the accrual of interest was suspended on the loan prior to the modification or if the payment amount significantly increased subsequent to the modification, the loan would remain on nonaccrual status until the borrower demonstrates the willingness and the ability to make the restructured loan payments for a period of six consecutive months.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Calibri,sans-serif;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div is classified as a foreclosed asset until it is sold.&#160;&#160;When property is acquired, it is recorded at fair value, net of estimated selling expenses.&#160;&#160;Holding costs and declines in fair value after acquisition of the property result in charges to earnings.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><font
